claims.claim: Every rational input flow x has a polynomial-size rational source-to-sink path decomposition, whose total weight q_st for each ordered pair (s,t) satisfies q_st<=d_t<=d_max.
claims.evidence: Adding a supersource arc of value b(s) to each source and a supersink arc of value d_t from each sink gives a conserved acyclic flow. Repeatedly subtracting the minimum positive value on a supersource-to-supersink path zeros at least one arc, so at most |A|+|S+|+|S-| paths are produced. Stripping the added arcs yields source-to-sink paths. The paths ending at t have total weight exactly d_t, hence q_st<=d_t<=d_max. Exact rational subtraction preserves polynomial encoding length because only polynomially many operations occur on input rationals.
claims.search_method: Direct proof using acyclic flow decomposition and rational bit-length bounds.

claims.claim: After fixing the pair weights q_st, choosing one supported path P_st for every positive pair and assigning it weight q_st always produces a nonnegative unsplittable b-transshipment.
claims.evidence: A weighted s-to-t path has divergence +q_st at s, -q_st at t, and zero elsewhere. The grouped decomposition has source row sums b(s) and sink column sums d_t, so the selected paths have balance b and are nonnegative, with one path per positive pair. Selecting a group path P with probability f_P/q_st contributes expected incidence f_P, so summing over groups gives E[Y_a]=x_a exactly.

claims.claim: On rational inputs, any real feasible unsplittable solution can be replaced by one with polynomially bounded rational encoding; consequently, existence is in NP.
claims.evidence: Fix the at-most |S+||S-| paths used by a real solution. Their weights satisfy a rational linear system consisting of nonnegativity, rational row and column equalities, and rational arc inequalities. Each weight is bounded by its source supply, so this polytope is bounded. A nonempty bounded rational polytope has a rational basic feasible solution; Cramer's rule and Hadamard's bound give polynomial numerator and denominator bit lengths because the dimension and coefficient bit lengths are polynomial. The paths and these weights are an exact polynomial-size certificate.

claims.claim: The facts q_st<=d_max and E[Y]=x are insufficient by themselves for arbitrary grouped incidence vectors.
claims.evidence: With d_max=1, two unit groups independently choose one of three rows and one of three columns of a 3-by-3 coordinate array. Uniform marginals give x_ij=2/3. Every deterministic row-column choice has y_ij=2 at their intersection, so its discrepancy there is 4/3>1. The integer checker enumerated all nine choices and confirmed that their minimum maximum discrepancy is 4/3.
claims.search_method: Complete integer-scaled enumeration of the nine row-column outcomes.
claims.witness: Two weight-one groups with choices R_1,R_2,R_3 and C_1,C_2,C_3; every pair (R_i,C_j) has y_ij=2 while x_ij=2/3.

claims.claim: A dominant-path residual gives an exact, efficiently checkable sufficient condition for the target.
claims.evidence: For group i, select a supported path of maximum weight f_i* and let r_i=q_i-f_i*. If an arc is on the selected path, the missing fractional weight is at most r_i; if it is not, all fractional weight using it comes from the other paths and is again at most r_i. On arcs where all paths agree, the change is zero. Thus |y_a-x_a|<=sum_{i:a in C_i}r_i. Checking whether every such sum is at most d_max and constructing the selected paths both take polynomial time.
claims.search_method: Per-group discrepancy proof followed by the triangle inequality.

claims.claim: If every pair group has at most h supported paths and total supply B satisfies B<=h d_max/(h-1), the exact target holds; in particular, two-path groups suffice whenever B<=2d_max.
claims.evidence: For the meaningful nontrivial range h>=2, a largest supported path has weight at least q_i/h, hence r_i<=((h-1)/h)q_i. Therefore every arc discrepancy is at most sum_i r_i<=((h-1)/h)B<=d_max by Claim 4's argument. For h=2 this becomes B<=2d_max. Groups with one path have zero residual and are trivially covered.
claims.search_method: Direct residual bound using the largest of at most h positive weights.

claims.claim: There is a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm producing an unsplittable y with max_a |y_a-x_a|<=min(B,sqrt((|V|-1)d_max B)).
claims.evidence: For independent group choices, E[Y]=x and E[sum_a(Y_a-x_a)^2]=sum_{a,i}q_i^2p_ia(1-p_ia). Conditional expectation fixes one group at a time without increasing this rational potential. Since q_i<=d_max and the expected length of a DAG path is at most |V|-1, the initial potential is at most (|V|-1)d_max sum_i q_i=(|V|-1)d_max B. Each coordinate error is at most the square root of the final potential. Independently, x_a,y_a are both in [0,B], giving the simultaneous bound B. All conditional expectations have polynomial-size rational descriptions.
claims.search_method: Exact conditional-expectation proof for the squared-error potential.

claims.claim: An expected-polynomial-time exact sampler improves the general relaxed bound to max_a |y_a-x_a|<=sqrt(d_max B ceil(log_2(4|A|))/2).
claims.evidence: For each arc, Y_a is a sum of independent variables taking values 0 or q_i, and sum_i q_i^2<=d_max B. Hoeffding therefore gives Pr(|Y_a-x_a|>lambda)<=2exp(-2lambda^2/(d_max B)). With L=ceil(log_2(4|A|)) and lambda^2=d_max B L/2, a union bound gives failure probability at most 2|A|e^{-L}<=1/2 because e^{-L}<=2^{-L}<=1/(4|A|). Exact rational categorical sampling and the squared rational acceptance test are expected-polynomial-time; the expected number of trials is at most two.
claims.search_method: Exact Hoeffding and union-bound calculation plus rational rejection-sampling analysis.

claims.claim: If the positive-support digraph of x has at most one directed path for every ordered source-sink pair, then y=x is already unsplittable.
claims.evidence: Every positive-weight path in a decomposition of x uses only positive-support arcs. The uniqueness hypothesis therefore forces all decomposition terms having endpoints (s,t) to use the same path; merging their weights leaves x unchanged and gives at most one positive path per pair. Capped path-count dynamic programming on a DAG tests the hypothesis in polynomial time.

claims.claim: The exact target holds in polynomial time whenever there is only one sink.
claims.evidence: With one sink, total supply B equals d_max. Consolidating each source's decomposition terms onto one supported path preserves every source supply and the sole sink demand, hence gives an unsplittable b-transshipment. Both the original and consolidated flow on any arc lie in [0,B], because their total path weight is B, so |y_a-x_a|<=B=d_max. Decomposition and consolidation are polynomial-time exact operations.

claims.claim: Integral lower-and-upper flow feasibility lemma: if an integral-balance flow g lies between integral arc bounds l and u, an integral flow z with the same balances and bounds exists and is computable in polynomial time.
claims.evidence: Set w=g-l. Its required balances and capacities u-l are integral. The standard supersource/supersink feasibility reduction has a feasible fractional flow because g exists, and integral-capacity max-flow integrality supplies an integral feasible w. Then z=w+l is integral, has the original balances, and satisfies l<=z<=u. Standard max-flow gives polynomial time.

claims.claim: The exact target holds whenever b(v)/d_max is an integer for every vertex; this includes all single-source instances with equal sink demands.
claims.evidence: Let Delta=d_max and g=x/Delta. Its balances are integral. Integral-flow rounding between floor(g_a) and ceil(g_a) yields integral z with the same balances and |z_a-g_a|<1 unless g_a is already integral, when equality is forced. Thus y=Delta z has discrepancy at most Delta. Each sink has positive integer demand d_t/Delta<=1, hence exactly one unit. An integral path decomposition of acyclic z consequently has exactly one unit path ending at each sink, so no ordered source-sink pair repeats. With one source and equal sink demands, the source ratio is the number of sinks and all ratios are integral.
claims.search_method: Floor-ceiling integral-flow rounding and integral path decomposition.

claims.claim: For a single source and two sinks of scaled demands 1 and alpha<=1, there is a feasible integral two-unit flow z with lower bound 1 on H={a:x_a>1} and upper bound 1 on L={a:x_a<alpha}, with upper bound 2 elsewhere.
claims.evidence: Here 0<alpha<=1. Decompose x=f_1+f_2 by destination and put g=f_1+f_2/alpha. It has integral balances +2,-1,-1. On H, g_a>=x_a>1; on L, g_a<=x_a/alpha<1; and globally g_a<=2 because f_1 and f_2/alpha are unit path flows. Thus g satisfies integral bounds l=1 on H and 0 elsewhere, and u=1 on L and 2 elsewhere. H and L are disjoint. The integral-flow lemma therefore supplies the asserted z.
claims.search_method: Exact normalized-flow inequalities followed by integral-flow feasibility.

claims.claim: The exact target is computable in polynomial time for every single-source instance with at most two sinks, with arbitrary rational demands.
claims.evidence: The one-sink case is Claim 9. For two sinks, scale demands to 1 and alpha and decompose the integral z of Claim 12 into one unit path ending at each sink; route weights 1 and alpha on those paths. If z_a=0, its lower bound implies x_a<=1. If z_a=2, its upper bound implies x_a>=alpha, while x_a<=1+alpha. If z_a=1, y_a is either 1 or alpha, and for all x_a in [0,1+alpha] its distance from either value is at most 1. Thus every arc error is at most 1, including x_a=1 and x_a=alpha. Rescaling gives d_max, and all constituent operations are exact polynomial-time operations.
claims.search_method: Integral two-path decomposition and exhaustive three-case symbolic inequality check.

claims.claim: No counterexample exists in the finite SSUF classes exhaustively checked by exhaust_ssuf.py.
claims.evidence: The independent checker enumerates every forward-arc mask for canonical positive-support DAGs with vertex 0 as sole source and at most three terminal sinks, all demand numerators with maximum Q, all weak path-weight compositions, all distinct aggregate flows, and all one-path-per-sink candidates. Deleting inactive vertices and zero-flow arcs reduces any member of the stated class to such a canonical support graph. All comparisons use the integer condition |Y_a-X_a|<=Q. Runs through n<=6,Q<=3 and n<=5,Q<=5 both returned NO_COUNTEREXAMPLE, covering 5,046,888 and 182,554 path decompositions respectively.
claims.search_method: Independent exhaustive integer-scaled enumeration using the persisted checker.

target_evidence: The exact target asks for a polynomial-time construction satisfying the two-sided d_max bound on every rational acyclic instance. The draft explicitly states that it does not prove or disprove that universal assertion. It does rigorously establish material exact special cases: one sink, integral normalized balances, unique support paths, dominant-path residual certificates, and every single-source instance with at most two sinks. Its deterministic and randomized general results have weaker discrepancy bounds, and its finite search cannot establish the remaining universal case. In particular, arbitrary instances with at least three nonuniform sinks and general multi-source instances are not covered. Therefore the draft makes valid partial progress but does not fully resolve the target, exactly matching its claimed PARTIAL resolution.
